unit.why: A talmudic (Yerushalmi) tale of R. Abba bar Zevina, a tailor who refuses a gentile's demand to eat carrion, retold with a moral about loyalty to one's religion.

stories.start_quote: מעשה ברבי אבא בר זבינא שהי׳ תופר בגדים
stories.summary_en: R. Abba bar Zevina, working as a tailor in a gentile's house, refuses on pain of death to eat carrion; the gentile reveals he was only testing him and would have killed him had he eaten, since a man must be faithful to his religion.

tags.why: Praises the steadfastness of a talmudic sage, copied from the Yerushalmi

quotes: שהי׳ תופר בגדים בבית גוי אחד
ויאמר לו הגוי אם לא תאכל אני הורגך
tags.why: The plot is the sage's encounter with a gentile employer
Refusal to violate the prohibition of eating carrion

quotes: אם תרצה להרוג אותי הרגוני נא הרוג
tags.why: He withstands coercion to sin under threat of death

quotes: כי לא הי' בדעתו להעבירו על דתו רק לנסותו
tags.why: Concerns the halakhic issue of transgressing under duress

quotes: ואז הגיד לו הגוי כי לא הי' בדעתו
tags.why: The threat is revealed afterwards to have been only a test

quotes: כי האדם צריך להיות איש אמונים לדתו
tags.why: Framed with an explicit moral lesson on religious faithfulness
The story illustrates steadfastness and faithfulness to one's religion

missing_concepts: martyrdom / readiness to die rather than transgress (kiddush ha-shem)
consistency of religious identity as a moral
